LABEL: basement membrane of fallopian tube ampulla
Definition: An acellular membrane that lies adjacent to the epithelial cells of the fallopian tube ampulla mucosa, situated between the luminal epithelium and the underlying lamina propria of the ampulla.

LABEL: basement membrane of fallopian tube infundibulum
Definition: An acellular basement membrane that underlies the epithelium of the fallopian tube infundibulum, composed of basal lamina and reticular lamina that anchors the ciliated columnar epithelium to the underlying connective tissue.

LABEL: basement membrane of fallopian tube intramural segment
Definition: A basement membrane of epithelium that underlies the epithelial cells lining the intramural segment of the fallopian tube, the narrow tubular portion that penetrates the myometrial wall of the uterus.

LABEL: basement membrane of fallopian tube isthmus
Definition: An acellular membrane that is part of the epithelium of the isthmus of the fallopian tube, lying adjacent to the epithelial cells between the epithelial layer and the underlying lamina propria.

LABEL: fluid of fallopian tube ampulla
Definition: A bodily fluid that fills the lumen of the fallopian tube ampulla, providing the aqueous medium in which fertilization occurs and through which the oocyte and sperm move.

LABEL: fluid of fallopian tube fimbria
Definition: A bodily fluid that is located in or secreted by the fimbria of the fallopian tube, which may facilitate the capture and transport of the ovum from the ovary into the oviduct.

LABEL: fluid of fallopian tube infundibulum
Definition: A bodily fluid that is located in the infundibulum of the fallopian tube, which accumulates in the funnel-shaped opening where the ovulated egg enters the uterine tube.

LABEL: fluid of fallopian tube intramural segment
Definition: A bodily fluid that is contained within the lumen of the intramural segment of the fallopian tube, providing a medium for the passage of gametes and early embryos through this narrow tubular portion.

LABEL: fluid of fallopian tube isthmus
Definition: A bodily fluid that is contained within the lumen of the isthmus of the fallopian tube.

LABEL: inner muscle layer of fallopian tube ampulla
Definition: A circular smooth muscle layer that is part of the muscle coat of the ampulla of the fallopian tube. This layer forms the innermost component of the muscularis and, together with the outer longitudinal layer, generates peristaltic contractions that facilitate oocyte and embryo transport through the ampullar region.

LABEL: inner muscle layer of fallopian tube infundibulum
Definition: An organ component layer composed primarily of circularly arranged smooth muscle tissue that forms the innermost layer of the muscular coat of the uterine tube infundibulum, contributing to peristaltic contractions that assist in gamete and embryo transport.

LABEL: inner muscle layer of fallopian tube intramural segment
Definition: The innermost circular smooth muscle layer of the muscularis of the fallopian tube intramural part, which lies within the uterine wall and contributes to peristaltic contractions that propel the ovum toward the uterus.

LABEL: inner muscle layer of fallopian tube isthmus
Definition: A circular smooth muscle layer that forms the innermost component of the muscular coat of the fallopian tube isthmus, contributing to peristaltic contractions that propel the oocyte toward the uterus.

LABEL: intramural segment of fallopian tube
Definition: A subdivision of the fallopian tube that lies within the myometrium, the muscular wall of the uterus, connecting the isthmus to the uterine cavity. This is the narrowest and shortest segment of the fallopian tube, measuring approximately 0.7 mm in diameter and 1 cm in length.

LABEL: lamina propria Fallopian tube ampulla
Definition: A lamina propria that is part of the mucosa of the fallopian tube ampulla, consisting of a thin layer of loose connective tissue underlying the luminal epithelium and containing blood vessels and immune cells.

LABEL: lamina propria of Fallopian tube fimbria
Definition: A connective tissue layer underlying the epithelium of the fimbria of the fallopian tube, providing structural support to the fimbrial fringes that extend toward the ovary.

LABEL: lamina propria of Fallopian tube infundibulum
Definition: A lamina propria that is part of the uterine tube infundibulum, providing structural support to the mucosal layer of the funnel-shaped abdominal extremity of the fallopian tube.

LABEL: lamina propria of Fallopian tube intramural segment
Definition: A lamina propria that forms the connective tissue layer beneath the epithelium in the mucosa of the intramural segment of the fallopian tube, which is the portion of the uterine tube that passes through the wall of the uterus.

LABEL: lamina propria of Fallopian tube isthmus
Definition: A lamina propria that is part of the isthmus of the fallopian tube, consisting of a thin layer of loose connective tissue underlying the luminal epithelium.

LABEL: lymphatic of mesosalpinx
Definition: A lymphatic vessel that drains lymph from the mesosalpinx, the serous mesenteric fold extending from the fallopian tube to the ovary.

LABEL: mesothelium of mesosalpinx
Definition: A mesothelium that forms the epithelial lining of the mesosalpinx, the portion of the broad ligament surrounding the fallopian tube.

LABEL: middle muscle layer of fallopian tube ampulla
Definition: A smooth muscle layer that is part of the muscle coat of the ampulla of the fallopian tube, situated between the inner circular and outer longitudinal muscle layers. This intermediate layer contributes to the contractile function of the ampulla during gamete and early embryo transport.

LABEL: middle muscle layer of fallopian tube intramural segment
Definition: A smooth muscle layer of the muscularis of the fallopian tube intramural part, located between the inner circular and outer longitudinal muscle layers.

LABEL: middle muscle layer of fallopian tube isthmus
Definition: A smooth muscle layer situated between the inner circular and outer longitudinal muscle layers of the fallopian tube isthmus, contributing to the muscular wall that facilitates peristalsis.

LABEL: mucosa of fallopian tube ampulla
Definition: A mucosa that is part of an ampulla of fallopian tube. The mucosa of the ampulla is characterized by an extensive array of complex mucosal folds (plicae), and is composed of simple columnar epithelium containing ciliated cells, secretory cells, and peg cells overlying a thin lamina propria.

LABEL: mucosa of fallopian tube fimbria
Definition: A mucosal lining of the fimbria of the fallopian tube, comprising the epithelium and underlying lamina propria of the fimbrial fringes.

LABEL: mucosa of intramural part of fallopian tube
Definition: A mucosa that is part of the intramural segment of the fallopian tube. The intramural (or interstitial) part of the fallopian tube is the narrowest segment that lies within the myometrium, the muscular wall of the uterus, extending from the uterine cavity to where it opens into the broader isthmus of the tube.

LABEL: mucosa of fallopian tube isthmus
Definition: A mucosa that forms the innermost epithelial layer lining the lumen of the isthmus of the fallopian tube, comprising epithelial cells and underlying lamina propria.

LABEL: muscle layer of fallopian tube ampulla
Definition: A muscular coat consisting of longitudinal outer and circular inner smooth muscle layers that is part of the ampulla of the fallopian tube and is responsible for rhythmic peristaltic contractions.

LABEL: muscle layer of oviduct intramural segment
Definition: A muscular coat composed of smooth muscle tissue that surrounds the lumen of the intramural segment of the fallopian tube, the portion of the oviduct that traverses the uterine wall between the uterine cavity and the isthmus.

LABEL: muscle layer of oviduct isthmus
Definition: A muscular coat that is part of the isthmus of the fallopian tube, consisting of outer longitudinal and inner circular layers of smooth muscle that are responsible for peristaltic contractions propelling the ovum toward the uterus.

LABEL: nerve of fallopian tube ampulla
Definition: A nerve that innervates the ampulla of the fallopian tube, providing sensory and autonomic innervation to regulate tubal function.

LABEL: nerve of fallopian tube fimbria
Definition: A nerve that is part of the fimbria of the fallopian tube, providing sensory and autonomic innervation to the fimbrial region.

LABEL: nerve of fallopian tube infundibulum
Definition: A nerve that innervates or is located in the uterine tube infundibulum, providing sensory and autonomic innervation to the funnel-shaped opening of the fallopian tube.

LABEL: nerve of fallopian tube intramural segment
Definition: A nerve that innervates the intramural segment of the fallopian tube, providing autonomic innervation to this portion of the uterine tube where it traverses the myometrium.

LABEL: nerve of fallopian tube isthmus
Definition: A nerve that innervates and is part of the isthmus of the fallopian tube.

LABEL: nerve of mesosalpinx
Definition: A nerve that innervates the mesosalpinx, providing sensory and autonomic innervation to the serous mesenteric fold connecting the fallopian tube to the ovary.

LABEL: outer muscle layer of fallopian tube ampulla
Definition: A longitudinal smooth muscle layer that is part of the muscle coat of the ampulla of the fallopian tube. This layer forms the outermost component of the muscularis and works in coordination with the inner circular layer to produce the peristaltic movements necessary for transporting the oocyte and early embryo toward the uterus.

LABEL: outer muscle layer of fallopian tube infundibulum
Definition: An organ component layer composed primarily of longitudinally arranged smooth muscle tissue that forms the outermost layer of the muscular coat of the uterine tube infundibulum, contributing to peristaltic contractions that assist in gamete and embryo transport.

LABEL: outer muscle layer of fallopian tube intramural segment
Definition: The outermost longitudinal smooth muscle layer of the muscularis of the fallopian tube intramural part, which lies within the uterine wall and contributes to peristaltic contractions that propel the ovum toward the uterus.

LABEL: outer muscle layer of fallopian tube isthmus
Definition: A longitudinal smooth muscle layer that forms the outermost component of the muscular coat of the fallopian tube isthmus, arranged parallel to the long axis of the tube.

LABEL: plica of fallopian tube ampulla
Definition: An epithelial fold that is part of the mucosa of the fallopian tube ampulla, forming an extensive array of complex folds that increase the surface area for ciliated and secretory epithelial cells involved in oocyte transport and fertilization.

LABEL: plica of fallopian tube infundibulum
Definition: An epithelial fold that is part of the uterine tube infundibulum, comprising mucosal projections within the funnel-shaped abdominal extremity of the fallopian tube.

LABEL: plica of fallopian tube intramural segment
Definition: A mucosal fold that projects into the lumen of the intramural segment of the fallopian tube, formed by the elaborately folded endosalpinx characteristic of the fallopian tube mucosa.

LABEL: plica of fallopian tube isthmus
Definition: A mucosal fold that is part of the isthmus of the fallopian tube, formed by infolding of the mucosa to increase surface area.

LABEL: serosa of fallopian tube ampulla
Definition: A serous membrane that forms the outermost layer of the ampulla of the fallopian tube, derived from the visceral peritoneum and continuous with the peritoneal covering.

LABEL: serosa of fallopian tube intramural segment
Definition: A serous membrane that covers the external surface of the intramural segment of the fallopian tube, the portion of the oviduct that lies within the myometrium of the uterus.

LABEL: serosa of fallopian tube isthmus
Definition: A serous membrane that forms the outermost layer of the isthmus of the fallopian tube, derived from the visceral peritoneum.

LABEL: vasculature of Fallopian tube ampulla
Definition: A vasculature that is part of the ampulla of the fallopian tube, consisting of blood vessels that supply nutrients and oxygen to the ampullary tissue and support reproductive functions.

LABEL: vasculature of Fallopian tube fimbria
Definition: A network of blood vessels that supplies the fimbria of the fallopian tube, providing vascular support to the fimbrial fringe around the ostium.

LABEL: vasculature of Fallopian tube infundibulum
Definition: A vasculature that is part of the uterine tube infundibulum, consisting of the network of blood vessels supplying the funnel-shaped abdominal extremity of the fallopian tube.

LABEL: vasculature of Fallopian tube intramural segment
Definition: A vasculature that supplies blood to and drains from the intramural segment of the fallopian tube, the portion of the uterine tube that passes through the uterine wall.

LABEL: vasculature of Fallopian tube isthmus
Definition: A vasculature that is part of the isthmus of the fallopian tube, consisting of the network of blood vessels supplying this region.

LABEL: vasculature of mesosalpinx
Definition: The network of blood vessels that supply and drain the mesosalpinx, the serous mesenteric fold extending from the fallopian tube to the ovary as part of the broad ligament.

LABEL: wall of fallopian tube ampulla
Definition: An anatomical wall that bounds the ampulla of the fallopian tube, comprising the serosa, muscularis, and mucosal layers that define the structure of this dilated portion of the tube.

LABEL: wall of fallopian tube infundibulum
Definition: An anatomical wall that is part of the uterine tube infundibulum, forming the structural boundary of the funnel-shaped abdominal extremity of the fallopian tube.

LABEL: wall of fallopian tube intramural segment
Definition: An anatomical wall that surrounds and defines the intramural segment of the fallopian tube, consisting of mucosal, muscular, and serosal layers in the portion of the tube embedded within the myometrium.

LABEL: wall of fallopian tube isthmus
Definition: An anatomical wall that is part of the isthmus of the fallopian tube, consisting of the serosa, muscular layers, and mucosa.
